boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Nebraska-Lincoln, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend route that pairs campus orientation, art, outdoor space, recreation, and a few practical places to revisit during the semester.

cards.title: Start with the campus playbook
cards.subtitle: First stop: New Student Enrollment
cards.notes: Check the orientation resources before making plans, then use them to identify campus facilities, peer connections, and support you may want to revisit.
cards.short_summary: A structured introduction to Nebraska’s people, resources, and campus facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL describes orientation as a program that introduces students to peers and university resources that support success.
cards.access_notes: Orientation formats and dates vary; review the current New Student Enrollment information before attending.

cards.title: Take one unhurried campus lap
cards.subtitle: Next: make City Campus legible
cards.notes: Walk the core campus in daylight and note the buildings, green spaces, and resource locations you expect to use during your first week.
cards.short_summary: A self-directed way to turn a new campus into familiar landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL’s visit program describes campus tours with a current student and highlights places for studying, living, collaborating, and student involvement.
cards.access_notes: Use the official campus map and follow posted building-access guidance.

cards.title: Pause among the collection
cards.subtitle: City Campus art stop
cards.notes: Set aside time to look through the galleries at your own pace, then pick one work to remember as a landmark from your first weekend.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum stop centered on viewing art rather than rushing through it.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL states that admission to Sheldon Museum of Art is free.
cards.source_title: Sheldon Museum of Art opens fall semester exhibitions
cards.access_notes: Confirm current gallery hours and any holiday closures before going.

cards.title: Continue the art walk downtown
cards.subtitle: 1155 Q Street, near City Campus
cards.notes: Use the museum’s current exhibition information to choose a gallery visit, and leave time to look closely rather than treating it as a pass-through.
cards.short_summary: A free art museum near campus with rotating exhibitions and Great Plains-focused collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Great Plains Art Museum says it is at 1155 Q Street, is open Tuesday through Saturday, and has free admission.
cards.source_title: Great Plains Art Museum Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Tuesday–Saturday hours and notes closures for major holidays, university breaks, and home football Saturdays.

cards.entity_name: University of Nebraska State Museum at Morrill Hall
cards.title: Meet the campus natural-history museum
cards.subtitle: Morrill Hall, City Campus
cards.notes: Plan this as an indoor afternoon stop and check the exhibit schedule before you go, especially if you are visiting around a university holiday.
cards.short_summary: A natural-history museum with public exhibits in Morrill Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Morrill Hall lists museum exhibits open Tuesday through Sunday, with Monday and select holiday closures, and publishes admission information.
cards.access_notes: Check the museum’s current admission categories, hours, and holiday closures before arrival.

cards.title: Make a small group plan
cards.subtitle: Nebraska East Union
cards.notes: Bring your NCard, invite a few people, and reserve a lane if available; the official page says drop-ins are welcome but reservations receive priority.
cards.short_summary: An East Campus bowling stop designed for a casual group activity.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL says Husker Bowling Center offers free bowling and shoe rental for UNL students with an NCard, and is open daily.
cards.access_notes: Bring an NCard; confirm lane availability or reserve ahead because reservations and private parties receive priority.

cards.title: Add an East Campus food stop
cards.subtitle: East Campus Dairy Store
cards.notes: Check the posted menu and flavors, then plan this as a simple daytime stop while exploring East Campus rather than assuming a particular item is available.
cards.short_summary: A university dairy store selling student-made ice cream, cheeses, and meats.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL says the Dairy Store sells handmade products made by UNL students in its on-site plant and publishes current daily hours.
cards.access_notes: The store lists daily hours and specific holiday closures; verify them before making the trip.

cards.title: Take the garden loop slowly
cards.subtitle: East Campus Loop, north of 38th and Holdrege
cards.notes: Walk the arboretum’s paths in daylight, use the garden map to orient yourself, and treat seasonal plantings as a reason to return later.
cards.short_summary: A five-acre East Campus arboretum with trees, shrubs, prairie, and garden collections.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL identifies Maxwell Arboretum on East Campus, describes its plant collections, and states admission to the botanical garden and arboretum is free.
cards.access_notes: East Campus Gardens are listed as open daily from dawn to dusk; use marked paths and observe posted rules.

cards.title: Choose a future reset spot
cards.subtitle: 1625 N 38th Street, East Campus
cards.notes: Walk through the open and quiet study areas, then save the floor map so you know where to return when you need computers, a room, or focused time.
cards.short_summary: An East Campus library learning commons with open study areas, rooms, and computers.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL Libraries lists open study spaces, reservable and non-reservable rooms, and computer areas at Dinsdale Family Learning Commons.
cards.source_title: Dinsdale Family Learning Commons Study Spaces
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current location hours; reservable rooms require advance booking.

cards.title: End with a drop-in activity
cards.subtitle: Campus Recreation facilities
cards.notes: Check the building schedule, choose an available activity, and join a low-stakes drop-in session such as basketball, badminton, pickleball, or table tennis.
cards.short_summary: A flexible way to try recreational activities during regular facility hours.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL Campus Recreation lists open recreation opportunities including badminton, basketball, pickleball, soccer, table tennis, and volleyball during regular building hours.
cards.access_notes: Availability changes with building schedules and programmed activities; verify the current schedule and membership eligibility first.
